questions.stem: All of the following features are true regarding Hashimoto's thyroiditis except:

options.label: B
options.text: It is the most common cause of hypothyroidism iodine sufficient areas

options.label: C
options.text: Antibody against thyroglobulin and thyroid peroxidase is seen

options.label: D
options.text: It predisposes to the development of T-cell lymphoma

questions.answerText: It predisposes to the development of T-cell lymphoma
questions.solutionHtml:
It predisposes to the development of T-cell lymphoma
  • Hashimoto thyroiditis is not typically associated with the predisposition to the development of T-cell lymphoma but is associated with an increased risk of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 758

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas?
questions.solutionHtml:
Autoimmune hypothyroidism
  • The most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas is Autoimmune hypothyroidism, also known as Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
  • This occurs when the immune system attacks the thyroid gland, leading to inflammation and damage to the gland over time. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 757

questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old patient presented with features of hypothyroidism from 2-3 years, the histopathology is shown below. Based on histological features, what is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hashimoto’s thyroiditis
  • The given clinical history is suggestive of Hashimoto thyroiditis.
  • The histopathological image shows a mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate of the thyroid parenchyma, containing small lymphocytes, plasma cells, and well-developed germinal centres which are typical of Hashimoto thyroiditis. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 758

questions.stem: All of the following are features of De Quervain thyroiditis except:

options.label: A
options.text: In the early phase follicles are disrupted and replaced by neutrophils forming microabscesses

options.label: B
options.text: Inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and macrophages with granuloma formation

options.label: C
options.text: It is triggered by a bacterial, fungal infection

options.label: D
options.text: It is the most common cause of thyroid pain

questions.answerText: It is triggered by a bacterial, fungal infection
questions.solutionHtml:
It is triggered by a bacterial, fungal infection
  • De Quervain's thyroiditis is not triggered by a bacterial or fungal infection, but rather it is thought to be triggered by a viral infection.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 759

questions.stem: All of the following are true regarding thyroid adenoma except:

options.label: A
options.text: It is a solitary, spherical, and well-encapsulated lesion

options.label: B
options.text: Histological composed of uniform appearing follicles that contain colloid

options.label: C
options.text: Cystic change, calcification, and hurtle cell change are common

questions.solutionHtml:
Vascular invasion is commonly seen
  • Vascular invasion is a feature of malignancy, and its presence suggests a carcinoma rather than an adenoma. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 763

questions.stem: Which of the following thyroid tumour do not arise from follicular epithelial cell?
questions.solutionHtml:
Medullary carcinoma
  • Medullary carcinoma does not arise from follicular epithelial cells of the thyroid gland.
  • It arises from parafollicular cells (also called C-cells) of the thyroid gland, which produces and secrete calcitonin, a hormone that regulates calcium metabolism. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: All of the following are cytogenetic abnormalities seen in Papillary carcinoma of the thyroid except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mutation of RAS
  • Mutation of RAS is NOT a cytogenetic abnormality typically seen in papillary carcinoma of the thyroid.
  • RAS mutation seen in follicular carcinoma. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: Which unique translocation in follicular carcinoma forms the PAX8-PPARG fusion gene?
questions.solutionHtml:
(2,3)(q13,p25)
  • The unique translocation in follicular carcinoma that forms the PAX8-PPARG fusion gene is (2,3)(q13,p25).
  • This translocation creates a fusion gene composed of portions of PAX8, a paired homeobox gene that is important in thyroid development, and the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gene (PPARG), whose gene product is a nuclear hormone receptor implicated in the terminal differentiation of cells. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common variant of papillary thyroid cancer?
questions.solutionHtml:
Follicular
  • The most common variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma of the thyroid is the follicular variant


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: All of the following are histological features of papillary carcinoma of the thyroid except:

options.label: A
options.text: Complex branching papillae with fibrovascular core

options.label: B
options.text: Orphan Annie’s eye appearance and intranuclear grooves

questions.solutionHtml:
Propensity for angioinvasion
  • Papillary carcinoma of the thyroid generally does not exhibit a significant propensity for angioinvasion.
  • Follicular carcinoma of the thyroid is the subtype that more commonly invades blood vessels.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stemHtml: A 24-year-old patient presented with a thyroid nodule, and the ultrasound sound shows calcification. The histological features are shown in the diagram below. What is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Papillary carcinoma
  • The given clinical scenario with a histopathological image showing the presence of branching papillae with a fibrovascular stalk and cuboidal epithelial cells suggests the diagnosis of papillary carcinoma.
  • Additionally, calcifications on ultrasound are also commonly seen in papillary carcinoma. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: Which of the following are features of a diffuse sclerosing variant of papillary carcinoma?

options.label: A
options.text: Occurs in young individuals including children

options.label: B
options.text: There is extensive fibrosis throughout the gland

options.label: C
options.text: It is associated with lymphocytic infiltrate

questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • The diffuse sclerosing variant of papillary carcinoma is a rare subtype that typically affects young individuals, including children.
  • It is characterized by the presence of extensive fibrosis throughout the gland, which can make it difficult to diagnose.
  • Additionally, it is often associated with a prominent lymphocytic infiltrate.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: All of the following are histological features of follicular carcinoma except:

options.label: A
options.text: Capsular and vascular invasion is necessary

options.label: B
options.text: Histological show uniform cel forming a repetitive follicular pattern

options.label: D
options.text: Occasionally there is hurthle cell change

questions.solutionHtml:
Intranuclear grooves and pseudo-inclusion seen
  • Intranuclear grooves and pseudo-inclusion are characteristic of papillary carcinoma, not follicular carcinoma. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stemHtml: Histological examination of thyroidectomy specimen shown in the diagram, based on the histological features Identify the type of tumour:
questions.solutionHtml:
Follicular carcinoma
  • The histological features shown in the diagram suggest follicular carcinoma of the thyroid.
  • It is characterized by uniform-appearing follicles that invade the thyroid capsule and blood vessels, and have a propensity for hematogenous spread. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stemHtml: Histopathological findings of a thyroidectomy from an old patient with clinical presentation of a rapidly enlarging mass and symptoms of dyspnea, dysphagia, hoarseness, and cough are shown below. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anaplastic carcinoma
  • The given clinical scenario with a histopathological image showing spindle cells along with pleomorphic giant cells suggests the diagnosis of Anaplastic carcinoma.
  • Anaplastic carcinoma is a highly aggressive and rare type of thyroid cancer, typically occurring in older patients. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: All of the following are features of medullary carcinoma except:

options.label: A
options.text: It arises from parafollicular cells or C cells

options.label: B
options.text: It is associated with MEN 2A or 2B

options.label: C
options.text: RAS plays an important role in its genesis

questions.answerText: RAS plays an important role in its genesis
questions.solutionHtml:
RAS plays an important role in its genesis
  • RAS mutations are commonly seen in follicular thyroid carcinoma but not in MTC.
  • Instead, mutations in the RET proto-oncogene are associated with the development of MTC. RET mutations can occur sporadically or as part of an inherited syndrome such as MEN 2A or 2B. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stemHtml: Identify the tumour based on the histological features from a thyroidectomy specimen. Which of the following is associated with this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sipple syndrome
  • The given histopathological image shows abundant extracellular material deposition which suggests the diagnosis of Medullary thyroid carcinoma.
  • It is associated with sipple syndrome or MEN2A. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: Electron microscopy feature of medullary carcinoma of the thyroid is-
questions.solutionHtml:
Presence of dense granules
  • Presence of dense granules is the electron microscopy feature of medullary carcinoma of the thyroid.
  • Medullary carcinoma of the thyroid arises from the parafollicular cells (C-cells) which are responsible for producing calcitonin.
  • The tumour cells of medullary carcinoma secrete calcitonin and other peptides such as carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA). 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stemHtml: Based on the characteristic cytological findings in a 21-year-old patient who underwent FNAC identify the lesion:
questions.solutionHtml:
Papillary carcinoma
  • The FNAC image shows Orphan Annie eye nuclei, which are nuclei that lack pigment and resemble an empty ocular socket and the Presence of enlarged, irregularly shaped, and overlapping nuclei with nuclear grooves and pseudo inclusion suggests the diagnosis of Papillary thyroid carcinoma. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 764

questions.stem: What is the most common cause of endogenous hyperthyroidism?
questions.solutionHtml:
Grave’s disease
  • Grave’s disease is the most common cause of endogenous hyperthyroidism. It is an autoimmune disorder in which thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI) antibodies bind to and activate the thyrotropin receptor on thyroid cells, resulting in excess production of thyroid hormone.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 760

questions.stemHtml: Based on the histological features as shown in the diagram identify the thyroid lesion:
questions.solutionHtml:
Goiter
  • The given histopathological image showing distended follicles and colloid-rich glands suggests the diagnosis of Goitre. 


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 760
